answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging a slashable bond at entry: before an agent transacts, it locks value that peers seize if it duplicates another identity. Each fake node multiplies the cost, so an attacker's budget caps node count. The ledger keeps a cipher of each agent's proof of unique work, so a clone cannot mask a shared origin, and standing grows from a violet fringe of unverified peers to a dark umber baseline of proven effort, where independent attestations are required and cost fees. A hundred sybils means a hundred bonds plus attestation payments, all slashed on detection.
